rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the opponents cannot produce a surah like the Qur'an after testing themselves and their helpers, their inability proves its divine source, yet they persist in denial.
rows.anchor: إن لم تأتوا بسورة من مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will never be able to produce a surah like the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: أي لن تأتوا بسورة من مثله أبدا

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the challengers should summon their supporters to attest whether their attempted surah matches the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: «شهداءكم عليها إذا أتيتم بها أنها مثله مثل القرآن»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to call upon others means to seek their support and assistance; the cited verse illustrates calling for help.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {وادعوا} [البقرة: 23] يعني استنصروا واستعينوا.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that if they cannot meet the challenge, the truth has already been made clear to them.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا} [البقرة: 24] فقد بين لكم الحق "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must avoid entering the Fire by denying the Messenger's revelation after proof has shown it to be God's revelation and shown their inability to match it.
rows.anchor: بأنه كلامي ووحيي، بعجزكم وعجز جميع خلقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With an open wāw, waqūd is a noun meaning fuel like firewood; with a damma, wuqūd is the verbal noun for a fire burning.
rows.anchor: والعرب تجعله مصدرا، وهو اسم إذا فتحت الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stones are sulfur, which is among the hottest kinds of stone when heated, explaining why it is named as fuel alongside people.
rows.anchor: إنها حجارة الكبريت، وهي أشد الحجارة فيما بلغنا حرا إذا أحميت

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah reports that the stones are sulfur created in the lowest heaven when God created the heavens and earth, prepared for unbelievers.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله، في قوله: " {وقودها الناس والحجارة} [البقرة: 24] قال: هي حجارة من كبريت خلقها الله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that God made the sulfur stones as He willed.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن ميمون، عن ابن مسعود، في قوله: " {وقودها الناس والحجارة} [البقرة: 24] قال: حجارة الكبريت جعلها الله كما شاء

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأصحاب النبي
rows.claim: A report through Ibn Masud and a group of the Prophet's Companions identifies the stones as black sulfur in the Fire, used to punish its people alongside the fire.
rows.anchor: عن مرة، عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس، من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the stones are black sulfur stones in the Fire.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، " في قوله: {وقودها الناس والحجارة} [البقرة: 24] قال: حجارة من كبريت أسود في النار.

rows.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
rows.claim: Amr ibn Dinar says the stones are harder and larger than the stones people know.
rows.anchor: وقال لي عمرو بن دينار: حجارة أصلب من هذه وأعظم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that God created sulfur stones with Him as He willed.
rows.anchor: حجارة من الكبريت خلقها الله عنده كيف شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire is prepared for those who deny God as their sole Lord and Creator, despite His provision of the earth and sustenance, and who associate partners with Him in worship.
rows.anchor: المشركين معه في عبادته الأنداد والآلهة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the warning applies to whoever holds the same disbelief as the people addressed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {أعدت للكافرين} [البقرة: 24] أي لمن كان على مثل ما أنتم عليه من الكفر "

rows.speaker: أصحاب النبي
rows.claim: A report from a group of the Prophet's Companions says people were nothing, then God created them, caused their death, and will raise them on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: عن ناس، من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah equates the two deaths and two lives in 40:11 with the sequence described in this verse.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله: " في قوله: {أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين} [غافر: 11] قال: هي كالتي في البقرة:

rows.speaker: أبو مالك
rows.claim: Abu Malik says God created them when they were nothing, then caused them to die and revived them; another report of his describes them as dead before God gave them life.
rows.anchor: عن أبي مالك: " في قوله: {أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين} [غافر: 11] قال: خلقتنا ولم نكن شيئا، ثم أمتنا، ثم أحييتنا "

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says they were nothing when created, then undergo the true death and are revived; he calls the wording in 40:11 equivalent.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد: " في قوله: {كيف تكفرون بالله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the passage about two deaths and two lives in 40:11 with the sequence in this verse.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " هو قوله: {أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين} [غافر: 11] "

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says God created them when they were nothing, then raised them, caused their death, and raised them at Resurrection; after that they return to Him.
rows.anchor: قال: حدثني أبو العالية: " في قول الله: {كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا} [البقرة: 28] يقول: حين لم يكونوا شيئا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by al-Dahhak, counts being dust before creation as the first death, creation as life, death in the grave as the second death, and resurrection as the second life.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " في قوله: {أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين} [غافر: 11] قال: كنتم ترابا قبل أن يخلقكم

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih's report from al-Suddi says that God gives life in the grave and then causes death.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، عن أبي صالح: " {كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they were lifeless semen in their fathers' loins, then God created them, caused the necessary death, and will raise them for Resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: " قوله: {كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا} [البقرة: 28] الآية. قال: كانوا أمواتا في أصلاب آبائهم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd reads the deaths and lives through the primordial covenant: God extracted Adam's descendants, gave them awareness and took their pledge, then formed them in wombs, caused death, and will raise them. He links this to 40:11, 7:172–173, 4:1, 39:6, 4:154, and 5:7.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " في قول الله تعالى: {ربنا أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين} [غافر: 11] قال: خلقهم من ظهر آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says each of the interpretations he has transmitted has an interpretive basis and approach.
rows.anchor: ولكل قول من هذه الأقوال التي حكيناها عمن رويناها عنه وجه ومذهب من التأويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic calls a vanished or obscure matter dead because its trace and mention have faded; a living matter is salient and known among people.
rows.anchor: هذا شيء ميت، وهذا أمر ميت؛ يراد بوصفه بالموت خمول ذكره ودروس أثره من الناس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari cites Abu Nukhayla's poem: reviving remembrance means making it famous, contrasting obscurity with a mention that is especially resonant.
rows.anchor: فأحييت لي ذكري وما كنت خاملا

words: وَكُنتُمْ أَمْوَٰتًۭا فَأَحْيَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading that 'dead' means unremembered, people were obscure in their fathers' loins, became known as living humans, died back into obscurity, and will be bodily restored with souls so they recognize one another at resurrection.
rows.anchor: فكذلك تأويل قول من قال في قوله: {وكنتم أمواتا} [البقرة: 28] لم تكونوا شيئا: أي كنتم خمولا لا ذكر لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is far-fetched to address people after they have been revived in their graves: the verse reproaches them for past crimes to call them back to repentance, which is impossible after death.
rows.anchor: ولا إنابة في القبور بعد الممات ولا توبة فيها بعد الوفاة.

words: وَكُنتُمْ أَمْوَٰتًۭا فَأَحْيَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatada's reading takes the first state as semen without souls, the first life as the breathing of souls into it, death as the soul's departure, and the final life as resurrection.
rows.anchor: فإنه عنى بذلك أنهم كانوا نطفا لا أرواح فيها

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd's account entails three lives and three deaths; al-Tabari rejects it as contrary to the text's two lives and two deaths and notes that no one claims an additional death at the covenant extraction.
rows.anchor: وزعم ابن زيد في تفسيره أن الله أحياهم ثلاث إحياءات، وأماتهم ثلاث إماتات.

words: وَكُنتُمْ أَمْوَٰتًۭا فَأَحْيَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view counts semen's departure from the man's body as the first death, its ensoulment and formation as life, death as the soul's departure, and resurrection as the second life.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: الموتة الأولى: مفارقة نطفة الرجل جسده إلى رحم المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari treats the semen-departure account as a possible interpretation only if it had been held by a recognized authority whose Qur'anic interpretation is trusted.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ووجه من التأويل لو كان به قائل من أهل القدوة الذين يرتضى للقرآن تأويلهم

words: وَكُنتُمْ أَمْوَٰتًۭا فَأَحْيَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas's reading: unremembered embryos became known as humans, died into unrecognized remains in the barzakh, and will be raised with souls before returning to God.
rows.anchor: القول الذي ذكرناه عن ابن مسعود، وعن ابن عباس، من أن معنى قوله: {وكنتم أمواتا} [البقرة: 28] أموات الذكر خمولا في أصلاب آبائكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari links the return and gathering to the resurrection scene in 36:51, where after the horn is blown people emerge from the graves toward their Lord.
rows.anchor: ونفخ في الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reproves hypocrites who profess belief in God and the Last Day while inwardly disbelieving and using the profession to deceive God and the believers.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية توبيخ من الله جل ثناؤه للقائلين: {آمنا بالله وباليوم الآخر} [البقرة: 8] الذين أخبر الله عنهم أنهم مع قيلهم ذلك بأفواههم غير مؤمنين به

words: كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَكُنتُمْ أَمْوَٰتًۭا فَأَحْيَٰكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari argues that the question challenges their denial of God's power to revive them after death, restore them after annihilation, and gather them for recompense.
rows.anchor: كيف تكفرون بالله فتجحدون قدرته على إحيائكم بعد إماتتكم وإعادتكم بعد إفنائكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reminds hypocrites and Jewish scholars of past favors despite their sins, warning of punishment like that of their predecessors while urging repentance for salvation at Judgment; he links their story to the warning at 2:6.
rows.anchor: يحذرهم بذلك تعجيل العقوبة لهم كالتي عجلها للأسلاف والأفراط قبلهم، ويخوفهم حلول مثلاته بساحتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following account of Adam shows God's honor to humanity, the consequences of disobedience for Adam and Iblis, mercy for Adam's repentance, and punishment for Iblis's pride and refusal to repent.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بعد تعديده عليهم ما عدد من نعمه التي هم فيها مقيمون بذكر أبينا وأبيهم آدم أبي البشر، صلوات الله عليه، وما سلف منه من كرامته إليه وآلائه لديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These stories address the People of the Book, who know them from their scriptures, and serve as evidence to them that Muhammad is God's messenger: he could not have learned their hidden accounts from books or their community.
rows.anchor: وخاصا أهل الكتاب بما ذكر من قصص آدم وسائر القصص التي ذكرها معها وبعدها مما علمه أهل الكتاب وجهلته الأمة الأمية

words: خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything on earth benefits humanity: it provides evidence of God's oneness in religion and livelihood and means in worldly life to obey Him and fulfill obligations.
rows.anchor: لأن الأرض وجميع ما فيها لبني آدم منافع. أما في الدين فدليل على وحدانية ربهم، وأما في الدنيا فمعاش وبلاغ لهم إلى طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun 'He' refers back to God's name in the preceding phrase, 'How can you disbelieve in God?'​
rows.anchor: وقوله: هو مكني من اسم الله جل ذكره، عائد على اسمه في قوله: {كيف تكفرون بالله} [البقرة: 28]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here creating means bringing the thing itself out of nonexistence into existence.
rows.anchor: ومعنى خلقه ما خلق جل ثناؤه: إنشاؤه عينه، وإخراجه من حال العدم إلى الوجود.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word mā functions as the relative pronoun meaning 'that which.'
rows.anchor: وما بمعنى الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made them living humans after they were semen in their fathers' loins, will kill and raise them for reward or punishment, and provides earthly livelihoods and proofs of His oneness.
rows.anchor: فمعنى الكلام إذا: كيف تكفرون بالله وقد كنتم نطفا في أصلاب آبائكم، فجعلكم بشرا أحياء، ثم يميتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayfa expresses astonishment and reproach rather than a genuine question, as in the Qur'anic phrase 'Where are you going?'
rows.anchor: وكيف بمعنى التعجب والتوبيخ لا بمعنى الاستفهام، كأنه قال: ويحكم كيف تكفرون بالله، كما قال: {فأين تذهبون} [التكوير: 26]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense clause functions circumstantially, with an understood qad omitted because the context signals it, as in 4:90 and ordinary Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: وحل قوله: {وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم} [البقرة: 28] محل الحال، وفيه إضمار قد، ولكنها حذفت لما في الكلام من الدليل عليها.

words: خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains that God subjected everything on earth for humanity.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: " قوله: {هو الذي خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا} [البقرة: 29] نعم والله سخر لكم ما في الأرض "
